intro: You're looking for a scale and polish near you, probably because you want your teeth cleaned professionally and you'd rather not travel far. Whether it's been a while since your last clean or you've noticed some tartar building up, a private dentist or hygienist can remove it and give you advice on keeping your gums healthy. We can introduce you to a suitable UK professional in your area who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a scale and polish usually need
need_lead: Most people want a straightforward, local appointment to get their teeth cleaned and their gums checked.
needs: You've noticed hardened plaque or tartar along your gum line and want it removed before it causes problems.
Your gums bleed when you brush or floss, and you'd like a professional to take a look and clean your teeth.
It's been a long time since your last dental clean and you'd like to get back into a good routine.
You're getting married, going for an interview or have another event coming up and want your mouth to feel fresher.
You've been told by your dentist that you need a scale and polish but you'd prefer to see someone closer to home or at a time that suits you.
context_heading: What a scale and polish involves
context: A scale and polish removes plaque and tartar from your teeth, which helps prevent gum disease and freshens your mouth. It's usually carried out by a dental hygienist, though a dentist may do it too. How often you need one depends on the health of your gums, so the professional will assess you and advise on the right interval.

It's common to feel some sensitivity after a cleaning, especially if you haven't had one for a while. This usually settles down, but you can ask the professional about it beforehand. Dentists, dental hygienists, dental therapists and dental nurses must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the GDC register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales it's Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you're looking for a scale and polish and say where you are based, so we can introduce you to a professional nearby.
Say when you last had a dental check-up or a clean, as this helps the professional understand your situation.
Describe any gum symptoms you've noticed, such as bleeding, swelling or tenderness.
Let us know if you have any particular concerns about sensitivity or if you've had a bad experience with cleaning before.
Tell us if you have a preference for a particular day or time, such as evenings or weekends.
Mention if you're registered with an NHS dentist but are choosing to see a private professional for this treatment.
questions: Will you or a hygienist carry out the scale and polish?
How often do you recommend I have a scale and polish based on my gum health?
What can I expect in terms of sensitivity afterwards, and how should I manage it?
Will you show me the best way to brush and floss to help prevent tartar building up again?
What is the fee for a scale and polish, and are there any extra costs?
If I need further treatment, such as a deeper clean, what would that involve?

faqs.q: Is a scale and polish painful?
faqs.a: Most people find it comfortable, though you may feel some vibration or scraping. If your gums are inflamed or you have a lot of tartar, it can be a little tender, but the professional will go at your pace. Let them know if you feel any discomfort.

faqs.q: How long does a scale and polish take?
faqs.a: It depends on how much tartar and plaque there is, but a routine clean usually takes a short appointment. The professional will be able to give you an idea when you book.

faqs.q: Can a hygienist do a scale and polish?
faqs.a: Yes, dental hygienists are trained to carry out scale and polish treatments. They must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the register online. Some practices may have a dentist do it instead.

faqs.q: What should I do if I'm not happy with the treatment?
faqs.a: If something goes wrong with private dental treatment, start with the practice's complaints process. The Dental Complaints Service can help with private dental complaints that are not resolved.
